name: Druid Critter Chitterer
body:
While most druids get along well with animals, critter chitterers make a point of getting along with nearly every animal they meet. Possessing an uncanny knack for communication across the species and sapience barriers, they see allies where others see only pets, mounts, and livestock.

Class Features
Call of the Wild (Ex)

At 1st level, a critter chitterer develops a natural rapport with animals. This doesn’t take the form of a bond with a single animal, as it does with many druids, but rather an instinctual understanding of animal behavior that lets them communicate with almost any receptive animal.

As a standard action, the critter chitterer can temporarily teach an indifferent or better animal one of the tricks listed under the Handle Animal skill. Teaching an animal a trick this way does not require a Handle Animal check, although commanding an animal to use a trick still does. Any tricks learned with this ability are forgotten 24 hours after being learned.

This ability can affect a number of HD of animals per day equal to the critter chitterer’s class level and can be split between multiple animals.

At 5th level, the critter chitterer can teach an animal two tricks per use of this ability. They can teach an additional trick for every additional 5 levels after.

This ability replaces nature bond.

Tongue of Claw and Fang (Su)

At 13th level, a critter chitterer gains the ability to talk to animals at will, as though using speak with animals.

This ability replaces a thousand faces.

Savage Dominance (Su)

At 15th level, a critter chitterer can spend one use of their call of the wild ability to force their will on nearby animals. This functions as dominate animal with a target of one animal per level within a 15-foot radius spread. If one animal breaks the spell, the spell is not broken for the remaining creatures.

This ability replaces timeless body.

Call of the Wild, Book 1 – The Druid. © 2017 d20pfsrd.com Publishing; Author: Kalen Tessmann
